**Why it matters:** A visitor who follows one of these links reaches an error instead of the page promised.

**Likely fix:** Point each link at a page that exists, or bring the page back (or redirect its old address to where it went).

### MAJOR SITE-07: 2 links and buttons on 2 pages have nothing for a screen reader to say

**Why it matters:** A blind visitor hears only "link" or "button", with no idea where it goes or what it does; accessibility law (the ADA, the European Accessibility Act) counts it, and so do automated accessibility audits.

**Likely fix:** Give each one words: visible text, an aria-label, or an alt on the image inside it (an icon link to a cart: aria-label="Cart").

- /insurance/umbrella/: 1 link or button: `<a href="tel:+18557480537">`
- /claims/: 1 link or button: `<a href="tel:+18557480537">`

### MAJOR SITE-11: 1 page has no viewport setting

**Why it matters:** On a phone a page with no viewport setting is drawn at desktop width and shrunk to fit, and Google ranks it as not mobile-friendly. A page that stops zooming fails people who need larger text (WCAG 1.4.4).

**Likely fix:** Use `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, without user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.

- /campaigns/leak-detection/www.beagleservices.com: no `<meta name="viewport">`: a phone shows the desktop page, shrunk

### MAJOR SITE-20: 256 scripts, style sheets and data requests on 251 pages failed to load

**Why it matters:** A script or style sheet that does not load leaves part of the page unstyled or not working: a menu that does not open, a button that does nothing, a list that never fills. Visitors see it; nothing tells the site's owner.

**Likely fix:** Point each at a file that exists (a path changed in a release is the usual cause), or remove the reference.

### MAJOR SITE-21: The site's own scripts throw 202 errors on 83 pages

**Why it matters:** An error nothing catches stops the script that threw it: whatever it was doing (a form's checks, a cart, tracking) is left undone. Visitors never report it; it is seen only in the browser's console.

**Likely fix:** Open the page with the browser's developer tools, read the console, and fix each error at the line it names.

### MAJOR SITE-22: 250 pages are slow: the slowest took 26.4 s, without its images

**Why it matters:** Visitors leave a page that takes more than a few seconds, and search engines rank slow pages lower. The crawl fetches no images, fonts or video, so a visitor waits longer than this.

**Likely fix:** A slow first byte is the server: cache the page, or find the slow query behind it. A slow load is what the page asks for: fewer and smaller scripts, deferred until needed.

### MINOR SITE-03: 6 of the site's own links redirect before they arrive

**Why it matters:** Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.

**Likely fix:** Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

- /agentlocator: 301, 301 to /agents/agent-locator/
- /local/california/homeowners-insurance/wildfire-mitigation/discounts: 301 to /local/california/homeowners-insurance/wildfire-mitigation/discounts/
- /local/california/homeowners-insurance/wildfire-mitigation/minimum-standards: 301 to /local/california/homeowners-insurance/wildfire-mitigation/minimum-standards/
- /sitemap.html: 301 to /sitemap/
- /claims/index.html: 301 to /claims/
- /campaigns/leak-detection/index.html: 301 to /campaigns/leak-detection/

### MINOR SITE-14: 1 page does not say its language

**Why it matters:** A screen reader guesses the language and may read the page in the wrong accent; browsers may offer to translate it wrongly.

**Likely fix:** Add lang to the html element: `<html lang="en">`.

- /campaigns/leak-detection/www.beagleservices.com: no lang on `<html>`

### MINOR SITE-15: 1 page has no main heading

**Why it matters:** Screen reader users jump to the h1 to learn what a page is, and search engines read it as the page's subject; none, or several competing, says neither.

**Likely fix:** Give each page one h1 naming what it shows; the site's name in the header is not it.

- /campaigns/leak-detection/www.beagleservices.com: no h1 shown

### MINOR SITE-17: 1 page has no description for search results; 4 pages share one

**Why it matters:** Search results show the description under the title; without one, the search engine picks a line of the page, often the menu or a cookie notice.

**Likely fix:** Give each page a `<meta name="description">` of a sentence or two saying what it offers.

- /campaigns/leak-detection/www.beagleservices.com: no meta description
- /resources/tags/homeowners-insurance.html: shares `Getting a quote with Mercury is fast and easy. See how mu...`
- /resources/tags/preparedness.html: shares `Getting a quote with Mercury is fast and easy. See how mu...`
- /resources/tags/catastrophe.html: shares `Getting a quote with Mercury is fast and easy. See how mu...`
- /claims/carsfirst/carsfacility/: shares `Getting a quote with Mercury is fast and easy. See how mu...`

### MINOR SITE-18: 1 address goes through a chain of redirects

**Why it matters:** Each redirect is another round trip before the page starts to load, and search engines may give up on a long chain.

**Likely fix:** Redirect each old address straight to the final one, and link to the final address.

- /agents/agent-locator/: /agentlocator → /agentlocator/ → /agents/agent-locator/ (301, 301)

### MINOR SITE-35: Requests to 2 hosts of other sites failed during the crawl, as seen from the crawler's machine and network

**Why it matters:** A script on the page asked another site's host for data (a third party's logging, analytics or a widget) and got an error or no answer. This was seen from the crawler's own machine and network only: an ad blocker, the region, DNS filtering or the crawler's own network can cause the same failure, and it may not fail for real visitors. The crawl cannot tell whether a page needs the answer. Where the crawl looked the name up from here, the line says so; "does not resolve" is stronger than "the request failed" (the host is probably gone), but it too is seen from here. It stops no build and no test.

**Likely fix:** If a name does not resolve, the host is probably gone: remove its snippet or tag from the site. Otherwise open the page from an ordinary browser and network; if the request works there, there is nothing to fix.

- /payment/one-time-payment.html: `c.go-mpulse.net`: 1 page asked it for data and the request failed; the name resolves from here, so the request failed for another reason
- /about/supplier-diversity.html: `cdn.acsbapp.com`: 1 page asked it for data and the request failed (404); the name resolves from here, so the request failed for another reason

### MINOR SITE-29: The site has no security.txt: someone who finds a hole has no way to report it

**Why it matters:** Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.

**Likely fix:** Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.

- /.well-known/security.txt: answered 404
